Description

  

    
Summary

A double-free vulnerability in kerberos_AcceptSecurityContext() and kerberos_InitializeSecurityContextA() (WinPR, winpr/libwinpr/sspi/Kerberos/kerberos.c) can cause a crash in any FreeRDP clients on systems where Kerberos and/or Kerberos U2U is configured (Samba AD member, or krb5 for NFS).

The crash is triggered during NLA connection teardown and requires a failed authentication attempt

Details

If kerberos_AcceptSecurityContext or kerberos_InitializeSecurityContextA() fails (due to invalid credentials or other premises not holding) kerberos_ContextFree is called to free up the allocated context.

kerberos_AcceptSecurityContext and kerberos_InitializeSecurityContextA() are called repeatedly and if this failure occurs after one successful call the PCtxtHandle might already be set to the value just deallocated.

Impact

This is a heap double-free vulnerability (CWE-415) in the Kerberos SSPI context cleanup path of WinPR, affecting all FreeRDP clients compiled with Kerberos support (WITH_KRB5=ON) on systems where a Kerberos realm is configured.

Who is impacted: any user running a FreeRDP-based RDP client (xfreerdp, wlfreerdp, sdl-freerdp, gnome-connections, remmina) or FreeRDP-Proxy on a machine that is configured for Kerberos authentication.

Affected versions: confirmed on 3.24.1 (latest). The bug was introduced with the addition of Kerberos support in FreeRDP 3.x and is present in all 3.x releases with WITH_KRB5=ON.

References:

User-facing report: https://discourse.gnome.org/t/still-can-no-longer-login-to-gnome-remote-desktop/34451

Fixed with

8078b8a
